image_description: A close-up, cropped view of a grey whale's back and dorsal area surfacing in turquoise water. The skin is dark grey with characteristic white mottling (barnacles/lice). Several dorsal knuckles are visible along the ridge of the back. No head, flippers, or tail flukes are fully visible due to cropping.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and blowholes are outside the frame; only the mid-back is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly shows the characteristic dark grey base with irregular white patches consistent with barnacle encrustation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no triangular dorsal fin. Instead, a series of small, rounded humps (knuckles) are visible along the dorsal ridge, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The extreme crop prevents assessment of the overall body shape or proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; texture and coloration are accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth and interior of the whale are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are submerged or out of frame.
